title: Lattice Structure and Efficient Basis Construction for Strongly Connected Orientations
summary: Let $\vec{G}=(V,E^+\cup E^-)$ be a bidirected graph whose underlying undirected graph $G=(V,E)$ is $2$-edge-connected. A strongly connected orientation (SCO) is defined as a subset of arcs that contains exactly one of $e^+,e^-$ for every $e\in E$ and induces a strongly connected subgraph of $\vec{G}$. Given a family $\mathcal{F}$ of proper subsets of $V$, we call an SCO tight if there is exactly one arc entering $U$ for every $U\in \mathcal{F}$.
